deep.reconstruction:
Setting. The page belongs to Grothendieck's axiomatics for an arrangement of pseudo-lines in the (projective) plane.
- 𝒟⃗ is the set of oriented pseudo-lines; |D| is the underlying unoriented curve.
- 𝒟⃗(s) is the set of oriented pseudo-lines through a vertex s.
- For an oriented pseudo-line D⃗ not through s, the operator ρ_{D⃗,s} acts on 𝒟⃗(s). The previous page (d) defines it: ρ_{D⃗,s}(Δ⃗₁) = Δ⃗₂, where Δ₂ is the pseudo-line through s whose intersection u₂ with D⃗ comes immediately after u₁ = Δ₁∩D. Here 'immediately after' means in the direction of D⃗, among the intersections of D with the pencil at s.
- So ρ_{D⃗,s} is a 'rotation by one step' of the pencil at s, with the sense of rotation read off from an auxiliary oriented pseudo-line D⃗.
- Point (c) of the previous page treats when two auxiliary lines D⃗, D⃗' give the same rotation.
- The next page states the goal: a uniqueness theorem. A system of operators ρ_{D⃗,s} satisfying axioms a)–f) is unique when the arrangement has no monogons or digons. It then induces a 'local system' Ω(s), i.e. a coherent local orientation / cyclic order at each vertex.

Point (e). Let D⃗, D⃗' be oriented pseudo-lines not through s, with distinct supports meeting at t. Let Δ₁, Δ₂ be pseudo-lines through s but not through t. They cut D at u₁, u₂ and D' at u₁', u₂'.
- (1) If u₁, u₂ are adjacent on D (no other pencil-line through s crosses D between them), then u₁', u₂' are adjacent on D'.
- (2) Orient D⃗ in the sense t→u₁→u₂ and D⃗' in the sense t→u₁'→u₂'. Suppose u₁, u₂ are adjacent in one of the half-lines (demi-droites) of D cut out by t, with respect to the pseudo-lines through s. Then ρ_{D⃗}(s u₁ u₁') = (s u₂ u₂'). Here (s u₁ u₁') denotes Δ₁ oriented from s through u₁ to u₁'.
- So the rotation step defined via D⃗ carries the oriented line Δ⃗₁ to the oriented line Δ⃗₂, with orientations transported coherently across both auxiliary lines. This is a compatibility axiom between the rotations defined by different auxiliary lines.

Point (f). If s has order 2n (n pseudo-lines through s, hence 2n oriented ones), then (ρ_{D⃗,s})ⁿ(Z⃗) = −Z⃗. Going n steps around the pencil returns the same pseudo-line with reversed orientation: a combinatorial 'half-turn'. This reflects that the oriented pencil is a double cover of the projective pencil.

Purpose. This is part of a program to extract from purely combinatorial incidence/order data on pseudo-lines a canonical local orientation (rotation system / local cyclic order) at every vertex. Uniqueness is to be proved under the nondegeneracy hypothesis of no monogons or digons.
errors: (1) is correct but stated more weakly than possible. n pseudo-lines through s cut RP² into n cells, each bounded by two consecutive lines of the pencil. A pseudo-line not through s crosses each of them once, so it visits these cells in the cyclic order of the pencil. Hence adjacency of u₁, u₂ on D just means Δ₁, Δ₂ are consecutive around s, independently of D; the hypothesis Δᵢ not through t is not needed for (1).

In (2) the hypothesis 'adjacent in one of the half-lines of D determined by t' is essential and is only sketched. Without it, the transported orientations on Δ₂ would disagree, cf. point (c) of the previous page. The intended statement is plausible but its proof is not written.
The notation Z⃗ in (f) is undefined on this page. It presumably denotes an arbitrary element of 𝒟⃗(s).

ideas.what: Rotation operator ρ_{D⃗,s} on the oriented pencil at s, defined by the order of intersections along an auxiliary oriented pseudo-line, plus compatibility axioms between different auxiliary lines
ideas.modern_name: Rotation systems / local cyclic orders at vertices of a pseudoline arrangement; local sequences; chirotope of a rank-3 oriented matroid
ideas.usually_credited_to: Pseudoline arrangements: Levi (1926), Ringel, Grünbaum (1972). Oriented matroids: Folkman–Lawrence (1978), Bland–Las Vergnas. Allowable/local sequences: Goodman–Pollack; Felsner–Weil (2001)
ideas.where_published: Unpublished; at most a general allusion in Esquisse d'un programme to combinatorial/tame topology

ideas.what: Adjacency on one transversal is independent of the transversal (the pencil at s has a well-defined cyclic order seen by every line not through s)
ideas.modern_name: Cyclic order of a pencil / local sequence at a vertex

ideas.what: Half-turn axiom: the n-th power of the one-step rotation reverses orientation at a vertex of order 2n
ideas.modern_name: Oriented pencil as double cover of the projective pencil (antipodal map on S¹)

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up an axiom system a)–f) for rotation operators ρ_{D⃗,s} on pseudoline arrangements. He aims to prove that such a system is unique (absent monogons/digons) and induces a canonical local system of orientations Ω(s). This is a combinatorial reconstruction of local orientation from incidence/order data, distinct in formulation from the oriented-matroid/chirotope and local-sequence approaches. The full axiomatics and the uniqueness proof appear not to be in the literature.
missed.quote: Alors ρ_{D⃗}(s u₁ u'₁) = (s u₂ u'₂). (f) Si s est d'ordre 2n, alors (ρ_{D⃗,s})ⁿ(Z⃗) = −Z⃗
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Of minor interest. It could be compared with Felsner–Weil characterizations of local sequences and with rotation-system descriptions of arrangements. Mainly historical: it documents Grothendieck's early-1980s combinatorial-topology program.

deep.surprise_reason: These are elementary, correct axioms about pencils in pseudoline arrangements, consistent with known combinatorics. The only unrecorded element is Grothendieck's particular axiomatic packaging and the uniqueness program; nothing would surprise a specialist.
transcription_corrections: First line: '𝒟⃗, 𝒟⃗(s)' should read '𝒟⃗ ∖ 𝒟⃗(s)' (D, D' not through s), matching (d) on the previous page.
The stray 'Δ' before '{t}' is a struck/false start, not part of the formula.
The inserted word above the struck 'ps droites' appears to be 'demi-dr.' (demi-droites, half-lines) of D, i.e. 'dans l'une des demi-droites de D'.
'les ps dr. qui passent par D' should be 'qui passent par s' by sense; the handwriting is ambiguous.
The struck-out fragment is an abandoned formula 'ρ_{D⃗}(s u₁ u₁'…', replaced by 'ρ_{D⃗}(s u₁ u₁') = (s u₂ u₂')'.
